headline: Warsaw Doctor Unveils New Universal Language, Calls It Esperanto
dispatch: A young Warsaw physician, Ludwig Lazarus Zamenhof, yesterday released a slim pamphlet introducing a constructed language he hopes all peoples of the world may share. Written under the pen name Doktoro Esperanto, the book lays out a grammar of just sixteen rules. Zamenhof, who grew up hearing four languages clash in the streets of Bialystok, has spent years crafting the tongue as a remedy for human misunderstanding.
answer: L.L. Zamenhof publishes the first Esperanto book, 1887
